basis: Enteric infections dominate yersiniosis; inflammatory intestinal involvement occurs in most cases across this group. Plague-specific organ involvement is not generalized.
Progressive conjunctival pterygium extending centrally over the cornea.
Epidermal nevus and major vascular malformations, including arteriovenous shunts and aneurysms, define the syndrome.
Staphyloma is an ectatic structural disorder of the sclera.
Primordial skeletal dwarfism and microcephaly define Seckel syndrome; microphthalmia reported in 1/1, supporting ocular involvement with limited sampling. Ectopic kidney is occasional.
Inherited retinal dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; both night blindness and Mizuo phenomenon occur in 6/6.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Lysosomal storage and dysostosis define the group; neurodevelopmental impairment or regression is common (>30%) across its predominantly neuronopathic disorders.
Classified as a pericytic neoplasm, involving the mural support cells of small vessels; no additional anatomical site is specified.
The definition specifies HSV-associated corneal stromal inflammation and necrosis. Herpetiform vesicles do not establish lasting skin damage.
Schistosomal infection directly affects the brain, spinal cord or meninges; other schistosomiasis sites are not universal to this subtype.
Intellectual disability, cardiac defects and skeletal/joint abnormalities define the syndrome. Coloboma occurs in 30-79%; hearing impairment also 30-79%, omitted at the four-axis cap.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A1 alone does not justify other organ labels.
Persistent eosinophilia defines the blood disorder; myocardial eosinophilic infiltration occurs in 30-79%. Pulmonary infiltrates and other documented organ lesions are occasional.
Vitamin D resistance causes hypocalcemia and rickets; alopecia affects roughly 50-70%. Hearing impairment in one reported patient does not establish a common manifestation.
Defective carotene-to-vitamin A metabolism; carotene-related skin discoloration does not establish skin damage, and ocular dysfunction is not documented.
Hamartomatous polyp arising in the stomach or intestinal tract; local inflammation does not make it an immune-mediated disease.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; severe thoracic restriction causes respiratory failure/asphyxia in most affected neonates as part of the defining phenotype.
Pleural tumor origin; invasion of diaphragmatic or chest-wall skeletal muscle is common (approximately 30% or more) over the locally progressive course.
Autoimmune inflammatory disease of muscle and skin. Interstitial lung disease is uncommon in the anti-TIF1 subtype (<30%); associated malignancies are separate diseases.
Congenital atrioventricular septal and valve malformation. Dyspnea is a symptom; recurrent respiratory infections are separately diagnosed infections.
Site-unspecified histologic umbrella spanning sarcomas, melanomas and carcinomas; no shared organ axis can be assigned without inventing an origin.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal/joint abnormalities characterize the syndrome; joint hypermobility in 20/20. JMML is separately diagnosed susceptibility; vascular frequency unclear.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss, metabolic dysfunction and myopathy define CGL4. Hepatic steatosis in 1/3 with reported liver enzyme elevation; cardiac frequency unclear, omitted at cap.
Acute metabolic dysfunction with encephalopathy/cerebral edema, hepatic fatty degeneration and hypoglycemia defines Reye syndrome.
